about: MMA's defaults, as data (docs/PLAN-start-a-game-gpt.md track L, L5 part 4a): a sport's standard scoring, lineup slots and locks, and the game specs a sport's Make it a game starts from instead of asking the bot. Stat keys are MMA's (src/lib/sports/mma.ts), one vocabulary for every promotion ESPN carries. Only the UFC's cards have ESPN's statistics (strikes, takedowns, control time, reversals): on the PFL's, LFA's and the rest, ESPN gives the result alone, so only a result's parts score there (the win's round, a decision, a quick win). The specs are in the game spec's shape; slots aren't in that schema yet (L4 adds them), so they're kept beside it for the spec to read.

scoring.source: DraftKings' MMA (its classic contests, as stokastic.com/articles/mma-dfs/ufc-dfs-strategy gives it on 2026-07-12 and rotowire.com/mma/article.php?id=54707 since its 2021 change; DraftKings' own rules page wasn't readable): a strike landed 0.2 and a significant one 0.2 more (0.4 in all), a second of control 0.03, a takedown 5, a reversal or sweep 5 (ESPN counts reversals; its sweeps aren't apart), a knockdown 10; a win in the 1st round 90, the 2nd 70, the 3rd 45, the 4th or 5th 40, by decision 30, and a quick win (in 60 seconds or less) 25 more. Nothing for a loss, a draw or a no contest. Left out: nothing of DraftKings' table; ESPN has no Fight or Performance of the Night bonuses, which no standard table scores

categories.source: DraftKings' MMA scores points, not categories (Yahoo, ESPN and FanDuel run no MMA game): none by default

slots.source: DraftKings' MMA: six fighters (any six: a card has no positions; its $50,000 salary cap isn't a slot)

season.about: A season of cards: draft 6 fighters, each scores on the nights they fight, most points over the season wins.

short.about: One card: everyone drafts a few fighters, every one of them scores, most points wins.

pickem.about: Each card, before it starts: who wins the main event? 5 points if you're right (a draw or no contest counts for nobody), most points wins.
